faq.q: What editing tools does it offer?
faq.a: Text (four fonts — Arial, Times New Roman, Courier, Georgia — with custom size 8–72 and colour), freehand Draw, yellow Highlight, White-out (white or black fill), Rectangle, Arrow, draggable Sticky Notes, and Image insert. Style presets quickly set these up: Review (red thin), Signature (black thin), Teaching (blue thick), Redaction (black-out) and Highlighter.

faq.q: How are my edits saved into the PDF?
faq.a: On Save, each page's rendered image, your annotation overlay and any sticky notes are composited onto a single canvas and embedded as a JPEG, then rebuilt into the PDF. This means the output pages become images — the original selectable text is replaced by a flattened picture of the page. It handles multi-page PDFs with page navigation and zoom (1x–4x).

faq.q: Can I pull the text out of a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. The "Extract All Text" button reads the text layer from every page using pdf.js and shows it in a panel labelled per page, which you can copy or download as a .txt file. This is separate from editing — it reads the existing text content rather than OCR, so it works on PDFs that already contain real text, not scanned images.

faq.q: What happens with a password-protected or damaged PDF?
faq.a: If the file is password-protected, it tells you to remove the password first; if it's corrupt or renamed from another format, it reports the file isn't a readable PDF rather than silently failing. For saving, it ignores encryption flags where possible. You can also Export ZIP to get each annotated page as a PNG plus the edited PDF. Everything runs locally in your browser.
